Parse lag(x, n = 1L, default = NULL, order_by = NULL) / lead(...)

Source: R/ir.R
ir_parse_shift_call.Rd

Builds a window-class ir_call(fn_name, list(x_ir), meta = list(n = , default = , order_override = )) node (never lowered directly – see the ir_call_registry entry / ir_bind()'s guard). n must be a non-negative whole-number constant (dplyr itself requires this); default, if supplied, must be a CONSTANT expression – evaluable via ir_eval_constant() with no data mask, so default = -1, `default = 2L

  • 3L, or any other column-free expression all work (not just a bare literal token), but default = first(x)` (a real, column-referencing dplyr default) is not supported.

Usage

ir_parse_shift_call(expr, env, schema, fn_name)

Details

order_by=, when supplied, must resolve via ir_parse_order_ref() (a bare column, desc(column), or -column); anything else (a general expression) is not supported and returns NULL. order_by= re-frames this spec's own frame exactly like order_by()/with_order() would if wrapped around the same call – see ir_parse_with_order()'s docs – so lag(x, order_by = y) and order_by(y, lag(x)) produce the same meta$order_override.
